The tape is punishing guides, not quarters (Williams-Sonoma -15%, Ross -7% and Intuit -12% after hours), so the three takes are reactions to today's own reports with something named to carry them: Valvoline long against retail, Williams-Sonoma short against retail, Intuit short outright. The rest of the screen is the defensive bid with no news of its own, breakdowns that are the tape or a story already three days old, and stretched names whose story is still running.

The AI and chip unwind runs on (SMH -2.8%, QQQ -0.8%, VIX 28.7 with the curve still inverted) while money rotates into the year's AI losers and defensives (IT services +3-5%, Dow and insurers up, 10-year back under 5%). The rest of the list is either the macro shorts the book already holds (precious metals, China ADRs, the AI unwind) or oversold names with no turn and no dated event, which the record says to leave alone.

Seventh straight S&P loss and a liquidation day (SPY -2.2%, QQQ -3.7%, SMH -8.3%, VIX 32, gold and bitcoin sold too): nearly every signal on the screen is one of two bets, defensives bid or AI beta sold, so I took only the two names with a story of their own (Takeda at a high on its launches, MasTec's debt-funded deal) and passed the rest as bets on whether the tape bounces.
